answer: Every identity must lock a bond that only returns in slow drips, like sap rising in a willow: thirty days of small releases, and any proven fraud forfeits the rest. A karst of cheap aliases collapses because each new name needs its own full bond, so a thousand clones tie up a thousand deposits while earning one identity's yield. Random audits — the saffron check — test a sample of past work, and a failed audit burns the bond, so faking a thousand histories costs a thousand deposits before a single reward lands.
